title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
statement: Return the LCA of values `p` and `q` in a BST. Both values exist, and all values are unique.
hints: The general binary-tree LCA is correct and does not use the BST property.
If both targets are smaller than the node, the LCA is in the left subtree.
If both are larger, go right. Otherwise the current node splits them and is the LCA.
editorial: Assume p <= q by swapping if needed. Walk from the root. A node smaller than p is too far left, so go right. A node larger than q is too far right, so go left. The first node that lies between them, inclusive, is the LCA, because one target is in each subtree or the node is a target.
